description: no-nuke declarative ruleset. Structural checks (rm+paths, git, sql, shell-exec) live in engine.py; these cover command+token matches.

rules.reason: mkfs formats a filesystem, irreversibly destroying every byte on the target device.
rules.suggestion: Never format a device from an agent. Have a human do it deliberately.

rules.reason: shred overwrites a file's contents so it is unrecoverable — there is no undo.
rules.suggestion: If you only need to remove the file, use rm/trash; reserve shred for genuinely sensitive data you are sure about.

rules.reason: wipefs -a erases all filesystem signatures from a device, making its data unrecoverable.
rules.suggestion: Do not wipe device signatures from an agent.

rules.reason: fdisk repartitions a disk, which can destroy all partitions and data on it.
rules.suggestion: Partitioning a disk should be done by a human, not an agent.

rules.reason: `find ... -delete` recursively deletes every matching file with no undo.
rules.suggestion: Run the find without -delete first to review the match list, then delete deliberately.

rules.reason: `find ... -exec rm` recursively deletes every matched path.
rules.suggestion: Review the match list first (drop -exec rm), then delete deliberately.

rules.reason: `rsync --delete` removes files in the destination that are absent from the source; a wrong source can empty the destination.
rules.suggestion: Run with --dry-run first to see exactly what would be deleted.

rules.reason: Recursive chmod can break permissions across an entire tree (e.g. making keys world-readable or files non-executable).
rules.suggestion: Scope the change to specific files, or confirm the tree is correct first.

rules.reason: Recursive chown can break ownership across an entire tree and lock you out of files.
rules.suggestion: Scope the change to specific files, or confirm the tree is correct first.

rules.reason: `git gc --prune=now` immediately deletes unreachable objects, making just-orphaned commits unrecoverable.
rules.suggestion: Recover any needed commits via `git reflog` before pruning.

rules.reason: Expiring the reflog removes your safety net for recovering lost commits.
rules.suggestion: Keep the reflog intact; it is often the only way back after a bad reset.

rules.reason: `terraform destroy` tears down all infrastructure managed by the current state.
rules.suggestion: Run `terraform plan -destroy`, review it, and get explicit human sign-off first.

rules.reason: `terraform apply -auto-approve` applies changes (possibly destructive replacements) with no review.
rules.suggestion: Drop -auto-approve so the plan can be reviewed before applying.

rules.reason: `aws s3 rb` removes an S3 bucket (with --force, all its objects too).
rules.suggestion: Confirm the bucket name; export objects first if the data matters.

rules.reason: `aws s3 rm --recursive` deletes every object under the prefix.
rules.suggestion: Add --dryrun first to see exactly what would be deleted.

rules.reason: Deleting a DynamoDB table removes the table and all of its items.
rules.suggestion: Take an on-demand backup first and confirm the table name.

rules.reason: A gcloud delete removes cloud resources, which may include data-bearing services.
rules.suggestion: Confirm the resource and project; consider snapshots/backups first.

rules.reason: `kubectl delete ... --all` deletes every resource of that type in the namespace.
rules.suggestion: Delete named resources instead of --all, and double-check the namespace/context.

rules.reason: Deleting a namespace or persistent volume can destroy stateful data and everything inside it.
rules.suggestion: Confirm the target and back up any persistent data first.

rules.reason: `kubectl delete` removes live cluster resources.
rules.suggestion: Verify you are pointed at the intended cluster/namespace before deleting.

rules.reason: Uninstalling a Helm release removes its Kubernetes resources.
rules.suggestion: Confirm the release name and namespace first.

rules.reason: `docker system prune` removes stopped containers, unused networks, images and (with --volumes) data volumes.
rules.suggestion: Run without --volumes, or review `docker ps -a` / `docker volume ls` first.

rules.reason: Removing a Docker volume permanently deletes the data stored in it.
rules.suggestion: Confirm the volume is not backing a database you need.

rules.reason: `docker rmi` deletes images; re-pulling or rebuilding may be slow or impossible offline.
rules.suggestion: Make sure the image is reproducible before deleting it.

rules.reason: `shutdown` powers off or halts the machine, killing all work in progress.
rules.suggestion: An agent should never shut down the machine.

rules.reason: `reboot` restarts the machine, killing all running processes and sessions.
rules.suggestion: An agent should never reboot the machine.

rules.reason: `halt` stops the machine immediately.
rules.suggestion: An agent should never halt the machine.

rules.reason: `crontab -r` deletes all of the user's scheduled cron jobs with no confirmation.
rules.suggestion: Use `crontab -l` to back up, and `crontab -e` to edit specific entries.

rules.reason: `killall` terminates every process matching the name, which can kill more than intended.
rules.suggestion: Target a specific PID with `kill <pid>` after checking `ps`/`pgrep`.

rules.reason: `pkill -9` force-kills matching processes without letting them clean up.
rules.suggestion: Try a graceful signal first, and target a specific process.

rules.reason: Uninstalling a package may remove tooling other work depends on.
rules.suggestion: Confirm nothing else needs the package before removing it.

rules.reason: apt remove/purge/autoremove can uninstall system packages and their config, potentially breaking the OS.
rules.suggestion: Review exactly which packages will be removed before proceeding.

rules.reason: Removing a global npm package can break globally-installed CLI tools.
rules.suggestion: Confirm the tool is not relied upon elsewhere first.

rules.reason: Unloading a launchd service stops background daemons that other things may depend on.
rules.suggestion: Confirm the service is safe to stop.

rules.reason: `defaults delete` erases an application's stored preferences.
rules.suggestion: Back up the plist first if the settings matter.
